input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When ANSI stripping applies, the added `.strip()` also removes all leading and trailing whitespace from the prompt, not just the escape codes the title describes.
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt on a non-TTY stream where stripping applies, for example prompt('Name') whose text ends in ': ' after suffix construction. Mechanism: `strip_ansi(text).strip()` drops the trailing space, so the prompt is written as 'Name:' instead of 'Name: '. Impact: the prompt output differs from the unstripped case by a trailing space, and the input text is not separated from the prompt. Only ANSI removal was announced, so this extra whitespace change is unintended.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: `.strip()` applied after ANSI stripping removes the trailing space from 'Name: ', so the prompt shows as 'Name:' on non-color streams. It also states the same effect, input glued to the prompt and output differing from the unstripped case.
